body:
ADLC P7 (distill) for the #284 / #309 session.

## Problem

CONTRIBUTING step 2 told contributors to run `npm test` before pushing. CI
blocks a PR on THREE required gates:

  npm test                                  (suite)
  node scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs origin/main   (rail-freeze + trust root)
  node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main    (mutation coverage)

Two of the three were documented nowhere and had no local entry point, so doing
exactly what CONTRIBUTING said still left a contributor surprised by CI.

Worse, there is an active trap: `adlc rails-guard` and
`scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` sound interchangeable and are not. The CI script
additionally forbids any change to an EXISTING ticket's contract in
.adlc/tickets.json (the rail trust root). The weaker check is the more
discoverable one.

This is not hypothetical. In the #309 session a branch reused a ticket id that a
concurrent session had already claimed on main, silently rewriting that ticket's
contract. `adlc rails-guard` reported "all checks passed" throughout; CI
rejected the PR. The gate did its job — the local workflow was the defect.

## Deterministic defense (preferred over prose)

1. `scripts/preflight.mjs` + `npm run preflight` — runs all three PR-blocking
   gates in CI's order, cheapest first, stopping at the first failure, after
   fetching the base ref (a stale origin/<base> makes both diff gates compare
   against the wrong tree and pass for the wrong reason).
2. CONTRIBUTING step 2 points at preflight and names the three gates.
3. `adlc rails-guard`'s clean-pass output carries a stderr advisory naming the
   stricter CI gate, so the friendlier command stops reading as full clearance.
   STDERR and human-mode only — stdout and the --json contract are untouched.

## Prose defense (only for what a script cannot encode)

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root — harness-agnostic, because this repo ships seven
harness plugins and a Claude-specific file would contradict that. Limited to
non-derivable, session-proven lessons: preflight vs npm test; ticket ids must be
re-read after a fetch AND checked against open PRs; never `git checkout --` a
file to undo a mutation experiment (it discards uncommitted work); check for a
concurrent agent session mutating the checkout; PRs are squash-merged so a
stacked base needs cherry-pick, not rebase.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `npm run preflight` exists and runs exactly the gates CI blocks on. Verify by
   a test that reads .github/workflows/ci.yml and asserts each CI gate marker
   has a corresponding command in preflight — so CI growing a gate reds the
   test rather than silently outdating the script.
2. preflight fetches the base ref before the diff-based gates, and fails
   (non-zero, with a clear message) when the base cannot be resolved rather than
   comparing against nothing. Verify by driving the real script with an
   unresolvable --base.
3. preflight stops at the first failing gate and exits non-zero.
4. A clean `adlc rails-guard` run emits a stderr advisory naming
   scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs, the .adlc/tickets.json rule that differs, and
   `npm run preflight`. Verify by driving the real bin.
5. The advisory does NOT appear on stdout and does NOT appear in --json mode;
   `--json` output still parses. Verify by driving the real bin both ways.
6. CONTRIBUTING names `npm run preflight`.
7. `npm test` green; `npm run preflight` green.

## Constraints

- rails-guard is an ENFORCEMENT package (trust-root tier): the change there must
  be output-only, with no effect on exit codes, violation detection, the --json
  document, or the manifest record. Per ADLC P5 this tier also requires a
  cross-model review recorded before merge — flag it rather than self-approving.
- Do not restate in AGENTS.md what CONVENTIONS.md or the code already encode.
title: Make the local gate set match CI, and record the working lessons agents cannot derive
